headline: A RMB1tn overnight repo and a tech-stock rout push the 10Y CGB to a 1-year low; 30Y leads again
summary: CGBs rallied on Tuesday as funding eased and stocks fell hard. The CCDC 10-year dropped 1.2bp to 1.626%, a new 1-year low below the 1.635% of Oct 20, and the 30-year led with a 2.2bp fall to 2.041% as TL futures rose 0.44%. The 2-year (−0.2bp) and 5-year (−0.4bp) lagged, so the curve flattened. Policy banks rallied a little less than CGBs at 10Y: CDB 10-year at 1.661% is 3.5bp over, ADBC and EXIM about 6bp and 5.5bp.
drivers: PBOC fills the overnight cap on MLF day

With RMB900bn of MLF maturing and month-end tax payments, the PBOC lent the full RMB1tn overnight ceiling plus RMB412bn of 7-day repos at 1.40%, a RMB1.01tn net injection. Shibor overnight fell 2bp to 1.281% and 1-month Shibor hit its lowest since May 2020, which backs the view that an overnight policy rate near 1.25% is coming on Nov 2.

The Shanghai Composite fell 1.33% to 3,648 and ChiNext 3.41%, with more than 4,900 stocks down as the AI-stock sell-off deepened (Reuters cites a 14-month low). Funds and brokers bought long bonds, so TL futures (+0.44%) beat T (+0.11%), TF and TS, and the 30-year fell almost twice as much as the 10-year.

Monday evening's redemption swap facility is read as the PBOC signalling that a disorderly bond sell-off will be stopped. That cuts the tail risk of fund-redemption spirals and helps duration and spread products, even though Cailian Press notes traders still lack a catalyst to break 10Y levels decisively.

September industrial profits rose 14.4% y/y against about 12% expected and 4.2% in August, the best since June. The gain came from AI hardware, metals and oil-linked prices, not domestic demand, so bonds looked through it.
data: A beat driven by AI hardware, metals and oil-linked prices, not households; bonds looked through it.
RMB700bn 1Y vs RMB900bn maturing (net −200bn); outright reverse repos +400bn net in Oct
A tidy-up, not tightening: medium-term liquidity is still up RMB200bn in October, and the overnight rate is now the policy signal.
Firmer growth, near the bottom of the 4.5–5% target. It eases pressure for stimulus but was not strong enough to sell bonds.
Growth is led by exports and AI-linked output, with households and property still weak. It does not challenge low yields.
CPI 0.9% (f 1.0%), core 1.0%; PPI 5.0% (f 4.4–4.5%), highest since Jun 2022
Cost-push from oil and AI components, not demand. Bonds ignore it unless core CPI follows.
New loans RMB1.08tn (f 0.98tn); TSF 3.55tn; M2 7.2% (f 7.4%); M1 3.2%
Loan growth is at a record-low 4.8% and money growth is slowing. Weak credit demand keeps banks buying bonds.
As expected. The policy signal now comes from the overnight-rate switch, not the LPR.
view: Mildly bullish for the next 1–2 weeks. I lower the expected CCDC 10-year range to 1.59–1.66% (from 1.60–1.68%) after today's break of the 1.635% low. Ample overnight liquidity, the BNSF backstop and weak equities favour bonds, but regulators have pushed back below about 1.62% before, and the long end has run fast, so I prefer the 10-year over the 30-year and still avoid the rich 5–7Y belly and policy banks against CGBs. An overnight policy rate set at or below 1.25% on Nov 2 or a soft October PMI would take the 10-year toward 1.60%. A stock rebound, a pro-growth plenum message or regulators' warnings would push it back to 1.65–1.66%.

buckets.name: CGB 1–2Y
buckets.why: The 2-year at 1.240% is in the 10th percentile of its year (average 1.313%), and the 1-year at 1.180% is now a touch below overnight funding after Shibor overnight eased to 1.281%. The front end already prices an overnight policy rate near 1.25% and lagged today's rally (2-year −0.2bp).
buckets.call: Hold; don't chase below 1.20% on the 2-year. Add only if the overnight rate is set below 1.25%.

buckets.name: CGB 5–7Y belly
buckets.why: The 2s5s10s fly is −16.9bp, in the 2nd percentile of the year against a −7.4bp average, and the 5-year (1.349%) and 7-year (1.446%) set new 1-year lows. The 5s10s flattener from ~29bp is working: 27.7bp today (62nd percentile, average 26.3bp), still short of the 25bp target.
buckets.call: Keep the 5Y-into-10Y switch (5s10s flattener) from ~29bp, target 25bp, stop 31bp.

buckets.name: CGB 10Y
buckets.why: The 10-year at 1.626% broke below its 1.635% low and is the lowest of the year, but against its neighbours it is still cheap: the 7s10s20s fly is −23.4bp, in the 88th percentile against a −29.4bp average. It remains the best value on the curve for duration.
buckets.call: Range 1.59–1.66%. Buy on a back-up to 1.65–1.66%; take profit near 1.61%.

buckets.name: CGB 30Y
buckets.why: 10s30s narrowed 1bp to 41.5bp, in the 22nd percentile and below its 45.5bp average, and the 30-year at 2.041% is at its 1-year low after leading two days running. Equity weakness and the backstop support it, but fast-money buying can reverse quickly.
buckets.call: Neutral. Add above 2.10% (10s30s ~46bp); poor risk/reward below 2.05%.

buckets.name: Policy banks 2–10Y vs CGB
buckets.why: CDB 10-year is 3.5bp over CGB, in the 3rd percentile against a 10.1bp average, and CDB 2-year and 5-year spreads (11.9bp and 9.5bp) are also near 1-year tights. The switch from ~3bp is open and slightly in the money as policy banks lagged the CGB rally; the new policy financing tools still need funding.
buckets.call: Keep the CDB 10Y into CGB 10Y switch from ~3bp, target 8bp, stop 1bp.

buckets.name: ADBC/EXIM vs CDB 10Y
buckets.why: ADBC 10-year yields 2.9bp more than CDB, in the 74th percentile against a 1.2bp average; EXIM is 2.0bp over, exactly its average. Monday's ADBC auctions were well bid, so the pickup looks like supply, not credit.
buckets.call: Hold ADBC/EXIM 10Y rather than CDB 10Y for the ~2–3bp pickup.

buckets.name: Policy banks 20–30Y
buckets.why: CDB 30-year is 11.0bp over CGB, the bottom of its 11.0–16.9bp range for the year and below its 12.8bp average (16th percentile), and the 20-year spread (6.4bp) is also at its 1-year tight. Policy bank long bonds simply tracked CGBs today, so there is no spread cushion left.
buckets.call: Prefer CGB 30Y to CDB 30Y; revisit policy bank long bonds above a 13bp spread.

cgb:1.note: Flat at 1.180%, now slightly below overnight Shibor (1.281%).

cgb:2.note: Down 0.2bp to 1.240%; lagged the rally, already pricing a ~1.25% overnight rate.

cgb:5.note: Down 0.4bp to 1.349%, a new 1-year low; still the richest point on the curve.

cgb:10.note: Down 1.2bp to 1.626%, a new 1-year low below the 1.635% of Oct 20.

cgb:30.note: Down 2.2bp to 2.041%, leading again as TL futures rose 0.44% to 118.53.

cdb:2.note: Down 0.3bp to 1.359%, about 12bp over CGB, a 1-year tight.

cdb:10.note: Down 1.1bp to 1.661%, about 3.5bp over CGB, near its 1-year tight.

cdb:30.note: Down 2.2bp to 2.151%, tracking CGB; about 11bp over, the 1-year tight.

adbc:10.note: Down 1.0bp to 1.690%, about 6bp over CGB and 3bp over CDB.

exim:10.note: Down 1.0bp to 1.681%, about 5.5bp over CGB and 2bp over CDB.

watch: Next: the Fed decision (Oct 28, early Oct 29 Beijing), the Fifth Plenum communiqué (Oct 29), October PMIs (Sat Oct 31), the end of the overnight repo series and the rate the PBOC sets when it switches (Nov 2), Hong Kong accepting CGBs as margin collateral from Nov 2, and October trade and inflation data in the following weeks.
